customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>"Aedon"</color>
Influenced by kuuvahki, many of Nod-Krai's creatures have followed a unique path of evolution, astonishing even the most seasoned of travelers.
Beasts that tread upon crackling thunder with floating horns, fruits that sprout from plant roots and scurry and hide, even gargantuan insects that could only be seen in ancient times.
Compared to these, a nightingale that ever glimmers with golden light hardly seems remarkable.
Illuga first encountered Aedon during a perilous mission. He had become separated from his squad and was lost in the endless expanse of a dark forest — though in hindsight, it was likely the Wild Hunt's mist-shrouded illusions, for the wilderness of Nod-Krai held no forest so deep.
Running through the darkness, he chased a faint glimmer, as it guided him out of the woods. Only when the moonlight pierced the mist did he see the light's source — a bird as translucent as crystal, radiant and pure.
From then on, the nightingale often traveled by his side, helping him deal with countless problems, and wherever he was stationed, Illuga would always leave a place for it by his door.
To Illuga, Aedon was a reliable companion. Even when he later learned from Alia that it had once belonged to the Torchforger, Solovei, it had little effect on him.
The creatures that dwell beneath the moon stand guard over this land — they who predate even the Lightkeepers. Long before humans set foot in Nod-Krai, they waged their endless struggle against the eternal dark.
In the story of the wick-bearing nightingales, the sun that illuminates the mortal world is, in fact, formed from countless birds carrying burning embers in their beaks.
Illuga felt that Aedon was a nightingale from that story. And one day, he too would become just like it — one bird among many.
Voice-Over

<color=#ffd680>Something to Share</color>
If you look north from the highest point in Piramida, you can just about make out the edge of the Snezhnayan tundra. They say that was the homeland of our first Starshyna, Torchforger Solovei. He ended up losing everything, even his home... Yet here, he found a place to belong. Maybe that's why this fortress exists — as a refuge for people like us, a place to find warmth in each other.

customize.text: Dialogues

<color=#ffd680>About the Lightkeepers</color>
The Lightkeepers were established to safeguard the freedom and peace of Nod-Krai. It was five hundred years ago that the Torchforger brought the first of the group together.
That said, there were moments over the years when it seemed we might fade into history. Our troop strength has, in turn, been rebuilt time and again.
But no matter what, as long as the light that symbolizes our will is not extinguished, we shall be reborn in flame anew.
<color=#ffd680>About Piramida</color>
Piramida is where we Lightkeepers are headquartered. Legend holds that it was founded by our first Starshyna, Solovei the Torchforger.
And before that, this was once the palace of the fae governor of Nod-Krai. In fact, you can still see the coat of arms from that era on the stone walls of the foundations.
If the stories are true, who knows, you might even uncover the fae governor's buried treasure.
Solovei

Silvestr Petrovich Solovei was born in the far north of Snezhnaya more than five hundred years ago and belonged to an illustrious family whose emblem was a nightingale, a mark of their distinguished heritage. Members of his family had once served as spies, but were elevated to the gentry by the Belyi Tsar. Originally, Solovei's elder brother had inherited the nightingale emblem, but he saw the Belyi Tsar and Hvergelmir's secret experiments to create the Primordial Human and was executed by the product of bio-alchemy, Zver, to prevent Solovei from revealing the emperor's secrets. And thus did Silvestr inherit the nightingale emblem and step into the royal palace, now mingling among the fae dignitaries of the court.

Since childhood, Silvestr had been friends with Avrelian, an orphan from Nod-Krai, the ideal heir to the Frostmoon Scions, whose mother had committed suicide, hoping that her son would never return to his homeland. As a child, Avrelian often spoke of his dream of creating an Elysium on earth and railed against the gods and the rich. One day, Avrelian and Silvestr persuaded Governor Prokhor Trubetskoy's five-year-old adopted son, Brahe, to reveal the location of his father's treasure. They played good cop and bad cop, using both carrot and stick to get him to talk, and Avrelian distributed the stolen wealth to the children of Nod-Krai. But they never learned that Trubetskoy had managed to recoup three times the amount in less than three days. Later, Solovei convinced Avrelian to walk away from the Treasure Hoarders, leave everything behind, and go to Snezhnograd to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar. However, he was promptly sent to his death without so much as a glimpse of the Tsar. During Avrelian's lifetime, Silvestr never understood his friend's idea, and only after he had become the notorious thief Reed Miller and was executed for his crimes did Solovei understand the true meaning of these words and decide to save this dream.

After Avrelian's death, Solovei, along with his nightingale companion, went to his friend's homeland, Nod-Krai, where he met twin sisters from the Frostmoon Scions, Aila and Alia. According to prophecy, they were the chosen ones, destined to bear the ideal heir who would lead the Frostmoon Scions to Elysium. The Archpriestess, Lovia, dreaming of realizing the plan to create the perfect heir, allied with the "mad monk" Rotwang, the Belyi Tsar's favorite. Over five hundred years ago, he was exiled from Khaenri'ah for studying forbidden dark knowledge. One day, he learned of the pitch-black Elysium beyond the heavens and was willing to do anything to reach it. Rotwang wandered for many years until he met the Belyi Tsar, who had a daring plan to seize the power to upend the world and become ruler of all living beings under the moon. On the orders of the Belyi Tsar, he went to Nod-Krai to obtain the power of the Moon, but the monk wanted to use it and the ideal heir to reach the pitch-black Elysium. Alia understood that Rotwang and Lovia's plan could lead to the deaths of countless people, so she pretended to be Solovei's close friend and gained his trust. When Silvestr decided to renounce his family name and drive away his bird, Alia took it in. To stop Rotwang, she sacrificed herself and sealed herself and the bird in the Pillar of Embla, through which Rotwang sought to reach the pitch-black Elysium. Although Solovei was unable to stop Alia, he was grateful for this sacrifice and sought to fulfill her final wish to support her sister, Aila. After her sister's death, Aila realized that the Archpriestess had deceived everyone and killed her to stop this evil, and Solovei left the Frostmoon Scions to uncover Rotwang's true intentions.

When
struck Teyvat five hundred years ago, the court of the Belyi Tsar could no longer mind the remote borderlands beyond the snowy plains. The horde of pitch-black beasts tore across the barren land, destroying all traces of past civilization. Countless souls lie buried within the ancient ruins, innumerable heroes faded where mists now stray. It was not until Silvestr arrived at the abandoned by the gods Nod-Krai. To combat the forces of the Abyss and the Wild Hunt, priestess Aila shared with Solovei, whom she saw as the hero meant to protect "Elysium," a sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions left by Hyperborea, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. It was capable of transforming the energy of the Light Realm and purifying the energy of the
Borrowing the priestess's power, Solovei raised that first beam of light and, in the name of the moon, banished the darkness to those lightless ruins, burying it deep down alongside the nightmare-torn souls. After Rotwang's first "death" at the Pillar of Embla, he returned as a being woven from the Abyss. Solovei and Aila were able to push the fiend and his followers back to Kipumaki Cliff and seal them there. Since Aila had the ability to see the future, she foresaw Rotwang's return from the impenetrable darkness, and Solovei decided to found an order that would meet the threat with Hyperborean technology. He named this order the Lightkeepers, in honor of the flame Aila had ignited, and he himself became the first Torchforger and the first Starshyna.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down...</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."</color>

When the Cataclysm ended, the survivors raised a lighthouse atop the mountains, where Governor Trubetskoy's palace had once stood, and their city, Piramida. To preserve his dear friend's pure, childlike dream, Solovei did not shy away from defending it before the new Archon, the Tsaritsa's court. The First Torchforger asked the Cryo Archon for autonomy for the borderlands, taking upon himself an oath of vigilance and sacrifice. And thus began the history of the "paradise" known as "Nod-Krai," and the Torchforger, bathed in the moon's eternal light, lit the everlasting flame and began his watch.

<color=#ffffffd9>"We shall part the snow-curtain of the sky, and blast the winter winds across the wasteland."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"We are the Lightkeepers, who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains."</color>

Solovei lived a long life, untouched by illness or misfortune, and trained many Lightkeepers. As he wished, his funeral was very modest, and no one shed a tear. And although Silvestr's old acquaintance, Brahe, attended the funeral, Moonchanter Aila never came. When Brahe went to see her on Hiisi Island, believing the priestess might not have known about the ceremony, he was met by a servant who timidly told him that Lady Moonchanter had long known of his arrival and what had happened to the Torchforger, but she did not wish to see him and asked him to return. The order founded by Silvestr Petrovich Solovei continued to exist after his death, protecting Nod-Krai from the Wild Hunt. Five hundred years later, when the seal placed by Solovei and Aila on Kipumaki Cliff weakened and Rotwang returned to the world for the third time, he was stopped by the Traveler and Illuga, who inherited not only the title of Lightkeeper but also Solovei's nightingale.

desc.text:
Dear Miss Aila,
I am truly sorry that I was unable to stop Miss Alia in that moment. Yet, it was through her noble sacrifice that we ultimately thwarted Rotwang and prevented the loss of countless lives. Now, I finally understand why she pretended to be my close companion. I hope to speak with you about this in greater detail when next we meet — though perhaps, by then, you will already know more about all this than I.
I shall not presume to judge, nor shall I attempt to alter your opinion of her. But I ask, if nothing else, that you allow me to honor Miss Alia's final wishes by sharing her words with you. She asked that I render all possible support to you (which I surely will. You are my benefactor, after all), and that — I relay this only as she spoke it — she hoped that you would go on to live a life of happiness and freedom.
As for the Arrow of Terpikeraunas you mentioned in your last letter, if it truly holds the power to dispel the pitch-black calamity, and if you are willing to share it with such selflessness, then on behalf of the people of Nod-Krai, please accept my deepest gratitude. Should, as you foresee, Rotwang indeed rise again from the pitch-black filth, then our successors — an order I am considering naming the "Lightkeepers," in honor of the flame you have kindled — will stand ready to vanquish the threat once more, armed with the technology you have so generously gifted us.
We can speak of the details in person whenever you are free. I understand all too well that, after Lovia's passing, the Frostmoon Scions have been left with countless matters demanding your attention.
Yours sincerely,
Solovei
